messages:
sara_support: FYI SimpleHealth reporting spikes of 504s on hosted inference for the last 2 hours. They say the SDK keeps retrying and they're seeing double billing. attaching sample logs and a curl they used.

customer-simplehealth: seeing ~10% of requests return 504 and then client retries 3x -> lots of duplicate tokens billed. no obvious pattern by model. hits spike around 11:20am UTC.

sara_support: sample curl they sent: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx' 
 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
 -d '{"model":"rwd-large-2025","input":"<long prompt...>","max_tokens":1200}'
```

sara_support: and SDK snippet (python):
```
resp = client.generate(prompt)
if resp.status_code != 200:
  # client retries internally 3x
  resp = client.generate(prompt)
```

alex_support: can you paste the x-request-id or the root request id from the payload? we need correlation id to check edge logs. also ask customer if they're using streaming or sync.

customer-simplehealth: x-request-id: req_0a9c7f2b. sync call (non-streaming). large prompt + embeddings call upstream (they do generate then embeddings in parallel).

luke_sre: tagged. i'll grep edge logs for req_0a9c7f2b and the 11:20-11:45 window. initial hypothesis: connection reset on the edge -> 504 to client while backend continued work. that can cause client retry loops.

maya_runtime: quick check: was there any recent kernel/runtime bump that could increase tail latency? @kai_infra any infra changes in that window?

kai_infra: deploy-bot shows a small proxy config rollout at 11:10 UTC (edge-keepalive-tune). pushing full configs at 11:12.

deploy-bot: deploy edge/proxy-config v2026.03.11-kv1 by kai_infra at 2026-03-11T11:12:03Z (gradual rollout 30%).

luke_sre: found entries: multiple connections from the customer's client IP where edge closed with FIN_WAIT due to idle timeout while backend was still streaming. backend logs show the worker completed generation and returned 200 internally ~1.8s after edge closed. sample lines: 
```
[edge] req_0a9c7f2b -> client: FIN_WAIT (keepalive idle timeout)
[backend] req_0a9c7f2b -> model: completed 200 in 1803ms
```

luke_sre: looks like the edge keepalive/tcp idle setting was lowered in the new proxy config and caused premature connection close for certain slow writes. customers using long prompts or embeddings+generate combos are most susceptible.

maya_runtime: repro steps i ran locally reproduces a 504 when I push a ~1.5s write pause on the server side and edge idle = 1s. repro script below: 
```
# simulate slow backend write
nc -l 8080 <<'EOF'
HTTP/1.1 200 OK\nContent-Type: application/json\n\n{"ok":true}
# but sleep before sending body to simulate pause
EOF
# curl with --max-time 10 to mimic client
```

maya_runtime: mitigation options: roll back proxy keepalive change (sets idle back to 5s), or increase backend streaming flush frequency (harder), or route affected tenants to alternate pool.

kai_infra: rolling back partial rollout now for the proxy-config to stop further exposure. patching full rollout cancel. ETA ~8m.

deploy-bot: rollback edge/proxy-config v2026.03.11-kv1 initiated by kai_infra at 2026-03-11T11:38:12Z.

sara_support: communicating to customer: told them to temporarily enable exponential backoff on SDK retries and to lower client-side retry aggressiveness until we confirm. asked if they'd like a temporary region failover (us-east).

customer-simplehealth: please do the rollback and we'll enable backoff. region failover would be helpful if easy.

luke_sre: after rollback, observation shows 504 rates fall back to baseline within 4 minutes. i can see per-tenant errors for SimpleHealth drop from 9% -> 0.6% p95.

maya_runtime: follow-up actions: (1) revert proxy change (done), (2) add integration test covering slow backend writes to catch in CI, (3) add tenant-level monitor that alerts when 504 rate > 3% for 5m. i'll file the runtime ticket.

sara_support: customer update sent: "we identified a recent proxy keepalive change that caused premature connection closes for some long-payload requests. we've rolled back the change and recommend you enable exponential backoff for retries; we'll follow up with a patch and CI test." customer is OK with that message.

kai_infra: creating postmortem draft and marking the proxy config as blocked until tests added.

alex_support: will follow up with billing ops about duplicate token billing for retry storms — assigned to billing-team-queue.

sara_support: moving to resolved for now. scheduled follow-up call with SimpleHealth on 2026-03-12 16:00 UTC to verify no regressions. thanks everyone :slightly_smiling_face:

customer-simplehealth: thanks for the quick response and the rollback, appreciate it.
